newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Euro Court widens public access to information.
newsitem.headline: Euro Court widens public access to information.

text.p: The European Court told the European Commission on Wednesday it cannot deny the public access to information on the general basis of a need for confidentiality.

"This "catch-all" exemption allowed too much discretion to the Commission," said a lawyer for the World Wide Fund for Nature. "Today's Court decision begins to set out some more reasonable boundaries to protect the citizen's rights to open government."
The WWF took the Commission to the European Court of First Instance to force them to reveal information used in deciding not to fund a national park project in Western Ireland.
"This is an important victory for all who want to see more openness in European decision-making," said Tony Long, Director of WWF's European Policy Office.

The court said the Commission must strike a genuine balance between the public's need to know and its own interest in protecting the privacy of its deliberations. If it chose to withhold documents, the Commission must indicate its reasons clearly and with sufficient detail.
When the Commission adopted its Code of Conduct on public access to information, it took on internal obligations relating to transparency, and conferred legal rights on third parties, the court said.
A Commission spokesman said it would analyze the decision over the next few weeks and decide whether or not to appeal to the European Court of Justice.
John Carvel of the Guardian won a similar case against the EU's Council of Ministers in 1995.
